title: Grateful Dead Live at Terminal Island Correctional Facility on 1971-08-04

ai_review.summary: High‑energy ’71 prison gig with Phil’s booming bass and a smoking Hard To Handle, captured on a mostly clear soundboard that suffers occasional bass distortion.
ai_review.review: The performance is quintessential early‑1971 Dead – tight playing, standout Hard To Handle, China Cat Sunflower → Rider and several Pigpen numbers that keep the energy high. The soundboard recording is generally clean and front‑loads Phil’s bass, but listeners note recurring bass distortion and a mid‑show buzz that detract slightly from an otherwise excellent capture.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating ~3.9, with the majority praising the show’s energy and song selection while noting only moderate recording flaws; weighted calculation yields a solid 4‑star overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear front mix with Phil’s bass prominent; occasional bass distortion on tracks like Big Boss Man and Sugaree, plus a noticeable buzz in the latter half of the set.

standout_songs: Pigpen songs (especially Hard To Handle and Next Time You See Me)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Starts a bit rough but quickly finds its groove; tight, concise set typical of 1971 prison shows with minimal jams yet strong song‑to‑song transitions.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone is praised as “tickling the chin” and his humorous on‑stage banter (“We are used to people breaking in”) adds flavor; overall solid lead guitar work.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass is repeatedly described as fat, funky, booming and occasionally distorted; he dominates the mix and drives the band’s momentum.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bobby is noted for his high‑note vocal moments, the Yellow Dog story, and occasional lyrical slips (e.g., on Playin').
band_member_comments.Keys: No keyboards are audible on this recording; the set relies on Pigpen’s harmonica and vocals instead.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming is described as steady, keeping focus throughout and providing a solid rhythmic foundation.
